text: You arrive at a bustling restaurant, hungry for a meal. You just want a table, a simple, reasonable request after a long day.
The host tells you there's a 30-minute wait, despite seeing several empty tables. A question mark hangs over your head.
You suspect they’re trying to seem exclusive, or the staff are just inefficient. This frustrating delay feels totally unnecessary.
What you don't see is the hidden flow. Those 'empty' tables are buffers: cleared, reset, or awaiting a server.
This buffer ensures kitchen flow and good server attention. No wait means chaos, rushed service, and a poor experience.
So, next time you wait, you’ll understand. It’s an invisible system ensuring your dining experience is consistently good for everyone.
